Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google's Best Wearable Yet

By Melissa Aguirre, San Francisco, October 14, 2024

Google launched the Pixel Watch 3 on September 10, 2024, at its Mountain View campus, and after four weeks of daily use I can say it's a meaningful upgrade over the Pixel Watch 2. The 45mm model I tested costs $399.99 and includes a brighter LTPO OLED display, rated at 2,000 nits, that finally holds up in direct sunlight along the Embarcadero.

Battery life is the standout improvement. Google claims 24 hours with the always-on display enabled, and in my testing I averaged about 22 hours before needing the charger. That's still short of the 48 hours Samsung promises on the Galaxy Watch 7, which remains this device's closest competitor.

The watch runs Wear OS 5 and integrates tightly with Fitbit, which Google acquired back in 2021 for roughly $2.1 billion. Sundar Pichai, Google's CEO, mentioned during the September keynote that health tracking would be the company's core focus going forward, a claim reinforced by new features like a loss-of-pulse detection algorithm built with input from cardiologists at Stanford Health Care.

Not everything is perfect. The charging puck is proprietary, incompatible with the Pixel Watch 2's cable, an odd decision given Google's usual push for standardization. Still, at this price, against the Apple Watch Series 9, the Pixel Watch 3 is the most compelling Android alternative I've tested this year.

Rating: 4 out of 5 stars.

DETROIT, Mich. — Reliant Motors Corp. announced Tuesday it will acquire Vantage Battery Systems Inc. for $780 million in cash, aiming to secure lithium-ion supply for its growing electric vehicle lineup. The deal, disclosed at a press conference at Reliant's headquarters in Detroit, is expected to close by January 15, 2025, pending regulatory approval.

Reliant CEO Marcus Whitfield said the acquisition would let the automaker control production of battery cells used in the Reliant Voltra, its flagship electric sedan. "This gives us direct oversight of a critical supply chain," Whitfield told reporters. Vantage Battery Systems, headquartered in Austin, Texas, was founded in 2016 by engineer Priya Nandakumar, who will join Reliant as Chief Battery Officer once the transaction closes.

Shares of Vantage rose 22 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement, closing at $34.50. Reliant's stock dipped 3 percent amid investor concerns over debt used to finance the purchase. Analysts at Bramwell Securities estimate Reliant will take on roughly $500 million in new loans from Chase National Bank to complete the transaction.

The merger comes as competition intensifies with rival automaker Solara Motors, which last month unveiled its own battery plant in Reno, Nevada. Industry observers say the Vantage deal could narrow Solara's cost advantage in battery manufacturing.

Regulators at the Federal Trade Commission confirmed Wednesday they will review the acquisition for antitrust concerns before granting final approval.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Manchester City clinched a tense 2-1 victory over Chelsea on Saturday at the Etihad Stadium, with Erling Haaland scoring twice to extend his league tally to 12 goals this season. Chelsea's Cole Palmer had briefly leveled the score in the 63rd minute, converting a penalty after a foul inside the box, but Haaland's second strike in the 78th minute proved decisive in front of 53,000 fans. Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola praised his squad's resilience after the match, calling it "one of the most complete performances of the season." Chelsea head coach Mauricio Pochettino admitted his side struggled defensively, noting that the Blues conceded too many chances in the second half. The win moved Manchester City to the top of the Premier League table with 24 points, three points ahead of Liverpool, who play Arsenal on Sunday at Anfield. Haaland, who joined Manchester City from Borussia Dortmund in 2022 for a reported 60 million pounds, has now scored 9 goals in his last 6 appearances. City's next fixture is against Aston Villa on October 21 at Villa Park, while Chelsea will host Brighton on October 22 at Stamford Bridge. The Football Association confirmed no disciplinary action would be taken over a minor confrontation between players after the final whistle.

City will next travel to face RB Leipzig in the UEFA Champions League on October 17, while Everton return to Goodison Park to host Brighton on October 21. Ingrid Vasterling (born 14 March 1958 in Utrecht, Netherlands) is a Dutch structural engineer known for pioneering seismic retrofitting techniques used in bridge construction across Southeast Asia. She earned a degree in civil engineering from Delft University of Technology in 1981 and later joined Rijkswaterstaat, the Dutch public works agency, as a junior analyst.

In 1989 Vasterling emigrated to Singapore, where she began working for Keppel Engineering Group as a structural consultant. She was promoted to Chief Structural Engineer in 1996, a position she held for eleven years. During this period she led the redesign of the Meranti Viaduct following a partial collapse in 1994, a project credited with saving an estimated 40 lives in a subsequent earthquake in 2004.

In 2007 Vasterling left Keppel Engineering Group to found her own firm, Vasterling Structural Partners, headquartered in Singapore, with initial funding of 2.3 million Singapore dollars. The firm has since completed projects in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Vietnam, and by 2015 employed more than 150 engineers.

Vasterling married fellow engineer Willem Bakker in 1985; their son, Pieter Bakker, was born in Singapore in 1991 and now works as a project manager at Vasterling Structural Partners. In 2018, Vasterling received the Tan Sri Structural Excellence Award from the Institution of Engineers Singapore in recognition of her contributions to earthquake-resistant design. She retired from active practice in 2021 but remains chairwoman of the firm's advisory board.

DETROIT, Mich. — Automaker Falken Motors announced Tuesday that it will acquire electric-vehicle battery maker Voltrix Energy for $1.2 billion, in a deal expected to close by January 15, 2025. The agreement, disclosed at a press conference in Detroit, marks Falken Motors' largest acquisition since it was founded in 1987 by engineer Harold Renner. Falken CEO Marissa Cole said the purchase of Voltrix Energy, headquartered in Fremont, California, will help the company secure a stable supply of lithium-ion battery cells amid rising demand for its electric sedan, the Falken Aurora. Voltrix Energy was founded in 2014 by Dr. Anil Sharma, who will step down as Chief Executive Officer once the transaction closes and join Falken Motors as Chief Technology Officer. Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners estimate the deal will boost Falken's annual battery production capacity by 40 percent. Shares of Falken Motors rose 6.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while Voltrix Energy, which is privately held, does not trade publicly. The acquisition still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, a process expected to take roughly three months. Industry analyst Priya Nadella of Bloomberg Intelligence called the move "a defensive play against Tesla and Rivian," both of which have expanded battery manufacturing this year. Falken Motors employs approximately 18,500 workers worldwide, according to the company's most recent filing.

Frankfurt, Germany — Deutsche Bank AG announced on Tuesday that it has agreed to acquire a controlling 68 percent stake in Munich-based fintech firm PayLuxe GmbH for approximately 420 million euros. The deal, expected to close by January 15, 2025, marks Deutsche Bank's largest technology acquisition in nearly a decade. CEO Christian Sewing said the move would strengthen the bank's digital payments division as competition intensifies with rivals such as Commerzbank AG and N26. "PayLuxe's platform processes over 3 million transactions daily across Germany, Austria, and the Netherlands," Sewing told reporters at a press briefing in Frankfurt. PayLuxe co-founder Lukas Brandt will join Deutsche Bank as Head of Digital Payments starting February 3, 2025, according to a company statement. Brandt founded PayLuxe in 2016 alongside his sister, Anna Brandt, who will remain at the company as Chief Technology Officer. Shares of Deutsche Bank rose 4.2 percent on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at 15.67 euros. Analysts at UBS Group AG issued a note calling the acquisition "a shrewd bet on European fintech consolidation." The transaction still requires approval from Germany's Federal Financial Supervisory Authority, known as BaFin, which is expected to rule by early December. If approved, PayLuxe will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Deutsche Bank while retaining its Munich headquarters and 340 employees.

The deal, expected to close by Nov. 1, 2024, will make Boulder Grain Co. a wholly owned subsidiary of Rockwell Sierra Foods Inc.

CEO Martin Alvarez said the acquisition strengthens the company's push into the organic snack segment, which has grown 18 percent annually since 2021. "Boulder Grain Co. gives us immediate access to over 3,200 retail locations across the Rocky Mountain region," Alvarez told reporters during a press briefing at the company's downtown headquarters.

Boulder Grain Co. founder Priya Nair, who launched the company in 2011, will join Rockwell Sierra Foods Inc. as Vice President of Organic Product Development starting Oct. 1, 2024. Nair said she plans to expand the brand's oat-based product line into Canada by mid-2025.

Rockwell Sierra Foods Inc. shares rose 6.4 percent to $47.10 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while trading volume nearly tripled to 2.1 million shares. Analysts at Fenwick Capital Partners, including senior analyst Diane Osei, called the deal "a smart bolt-on acquisition" in a note to clients.

The transaction is Rockwell Sierra Foods Inc.'s third acquisition since 2022, following its purchase of Tallgrass Snacks LLC in March 2023 for $52 million.

input: Elena Marchetti (born 14 March 1957 in Bologna, Italy) is an Italian structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-retrofit techniques used in historic European buildings. She earned a degree in civil engineering from the University of Bologna in 1980 and later completed a doctorate at ETH Zurich in 1985. In 1991 Marchetti founded Marchetti Ingegneria S.p.A., a structural consultancy headquartered in Milan, Italy. The firm grew rapidly after being hired to retrofit the bell tower of San Marco Basilica in Venice following the 1987 regional earthquake assessments. In 2003, Marchetti Ingegneria was acquired by the Swiss conglomerate Baugruppe Holding AG for 42 million euros, though Elena Marchetti remained as the subsidiary's chief technical officer until 2011. That year she stepped down from the position to become a professor at Politecnico di Milano, a role she still holds. Her 1998 book, "Reinforcing the Past," remains a standard reference in the field of structural conservation and has been translated into English, French, and Japanese. In 2015, Marchetti received the Golden Compass Award from the Associazione per il Disegno Industriale in Milan for her retrofit of the Teatro San Carlo in Naples. She married fellow engineer Paolo Riva in 1983, and the couple's daughter, Giulia Riva, is now a practicing architect in Turin. Marchetti currently lives in Milan and continues to consult on preservation projects across the Mediterranean.

DETROIT, Mich. — Ferramotive Corp., the auto-parts supplier headquartered in Detroit, announced Tuesday that it has acquired Vantix Sensors Inc., a Palo Alto-based startup specializing in lidar chips for autonomous vehicles, for $340 million in cash. The deal, disclosed at a press conference on October 14, marks Ferramotive's largest purchase in its 62-year history.

CEO Marissa Holt said the acquisition would let Ferramotive supply sensor packages directly to General Motors and Ford Motor Company, both longtime customers. "Vantix gives us technology we couldn't build fast enough ourselves," Holt told reporters at the company's Woodward Avenue headquarters.

Vantix, founded in 2016 by engineer Rajiv Malhotra, employs 210 people and holds 47 patents in solid-state lidar. Malhotra will join Ferramotive as Chief Technology Officer starting November 1, according to a statement from the company.

Shares of Ferramotive rose 8 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $54.20. Analyst Tom Reiners of Everbrook Capital called the price "steep but justified," noting Vantix's technology could cut sensor costs by 30 percent within three years.

The transaction still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, which Ferramotive expects by January 2025. If cleared, Vantix will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary based in Palo Alto, retaining its current facility on Page Mill Road.

DENVER, Colorado — Aug 14, 2024 — Rocky Mountain Foods Inc., the packaged-snacks maker based in Denver, announced Wednesday it has acquired Boulder Crisp Co., a privately held tortilla-chip producer, for $142 million in cash. The deal, confirmed by Rocky Mountain Foods CEO Marisol Trent, is expected to close by October 1, 2024, pending regulatory review.

Under the agreement, Boulder Crisp founder Devon Ashcroft will step down as Chief Executive Officer but remain as a consultant through 2025. Ashcroft founded Boulder Crisp in 2011 in a small facility in Longmont, Colorado, growing it into a regional brand sold in more than 3,000 grocery stores across the western United States.

"This acquisition strengthens our snack portfolio and gives us direct access to Boulder Crisp's loyal customer base," Trent said during a press call Wednesday afternoon. Rocky Mountain Foods, which employs roughly 1,800 people, expects the combined company to generate $610 million in annual revenue.

The transaction will be funded through a combination of $90 million in cash reserves and a $52 million term loan from First Denver Bank. Analysts at Highline Capital Partners said the deal positions Rocky Mountain Foods to compete more directly with Frito-Lay in the western regional snack market.

Boulder Crisp's 240 employees will join Rocky Mountain Foods, and the company said no layoffs are currently planned. Shares of Rocky Mountain Foods, which trades privately, were not affected, though bondholders were notified of the new debt on Thursday, Aug 15.

CHARLOTTE, N.C. — Piedmont Bancorp announced Tuesday it has acquired Carolina Trust Financial for $412 million in cash and stock, creating one of the largest regional lenders in the Southeast. The deal, disclosed at a press briefing at Piedmont's headquarters in Charlotte, will bring Carolina Trust's 58 branches under the Piedmont Bancorp brand by early 2025.

CEO Marion Ellsworth said the acquisition strengthens Piedmont's presence in South Carolina and Georgia, markets where Carolina Trust has operated since 1987. "This merger positions us to compete directly with SunTrust and Wells Fargo in the mid-Atlantic corridor," Ellsworth told reporters.

Carolina Trust's chief executive, Daniel Ferris, will step down from his post effective December 31 after leading the bank for eleven years. He will be succeeded by Piedmont executive Renata Colby, who was named president of the combined entity's retail banking division on Tuesday.

Shares of Carolina Trust jumped 14 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $38.20. Analysts at Morgan Stanley called the deal "a logical consolidation" in a sector facing pressure from rising interest rates.

Regulators at the Federal Reserve are expected to review the transaction, with final approval anticipated by March 2025. Piedmont Bancorp, founded in 1962 by Harold Whitfield, employs roughly 6,800 people across four states.

The Ontario Ministry of Environment, Conservation and Parks announced on April 9, 2024 that it will provide CAD 42 million in grants to municipalities across the province for flood-mitigation infrastructure. Minister Andrea Kowalski unveiled the program during a press conference in Sudbury, stating that the funding responds to the severe flooding that struck the Ottawa River valley in May 2023, displacing more than 3,000 residents. Under the initiative, the City of Ottawa will receive CAD 8.5 million to upgrade stormwater systems near the Rideau Canal, while the Town of Pembroke will receive CAD 1.2 million for levee reinforcement. The ministry will begin accepting applications from municipal governments on May 15, 2024, with a submission deadline of July 31, 2024. Deputy Minister Farid Haidari said the program was developed in consultation with the Insurance Bureau of Canada and the University of Waterloo's Water Institute, whose 2023 report identified 214 high-risk communities along the Great Lakes basin. Kowalski added that a second phase, expected to allocate a further CAD 60 million, will be announced in early 2025 pending approval from the Ontario Treasury Board. Opposition critics, including MPP Diane Sutherland of the Ontario New Democratic Party, called the funding "insufficient" given that flood damages across Ontario exceeded CAD 700 million last year. The ministry will publish eligibility guidelines on its website by April 22, 2024.

Under the plan, the City of London will receive $9.5 million to replace the Greenway Wastewater Treatment Plant's aeration system, while Woodstock's public works department will use $3.2 million to install new stormwater retention ponds by October 2025. Kowalski stated that the province expects a 30 percent reduction in nutrient runoff within five years. The initiative was developed in consultation with Chief Leah Cardinal of the Chippewas of the Thames First Nation, who has advocated for stricter monitoring of industrial discharge since 2019. Environment Canada will conduct quarterly water-quality testing beginning September 1, 2024, with results published publicly on the ministry's website. Opposition critics, including MPP Fatima Rahman of the Ontario NDP, welcomed the funding but called for a binding timeline to eliminate combined sewer overflows entirely by 2030. On March 6, 2024, Judge Rosalind Chen sentenced Marcus Feldman, 44, of Tempe, Arizona, to 63 months in federal custody after a jury found him guilty of securities fraud in connection with his role as Chief Financial Officer of Sonora Capital Partners LLC. Prosecutor Diane Whitfield, representing the Maricopa County District Attorney's Office, argued that Feldman diverted $2.3 million from investor accounts between January 2021 and September 2022, funneling the funds into a shell company registered in Nevada. The trial, held at the Maricopa County Superior Courthouse in Phoenix, Arizona, began on February 12, 2024, and lasted three weeks.

Defense attorney Harold Nunez maintained that Feldman had been unaware of the transfers, but jurors were unconvinced after reviewing bank records supplied by First Sonoran Bank. Sonora Capital Partners LLC, headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona, was acquired by Denholm Financial Group in 2019 and has since become a subsidiary of the larger firm.

Feldman was arrested on October 4, 2022, by agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation at his residence in Tempe following a six-month investigation. He is scheduled to report to a federal facility in Lompoc, California, on April 15, 2024. Whitfield told reporters outside the courthouse that the sentence "sends a clear message to corporate officers who betray investor trust." Feldman's attorney indicated he intends to file an appeal within 30 days.

MADRID, June 14 — Real Sociedad edged Villarreal 2-1 at the Reale Arena on Saturday, sealing a fourth-place finish in La Liga and a return to Champions League football next season. Midfielder Mikel Oyarzabal scored twice, including a stoppage-time penalty in the 91st minute, to lift Sociedad past Villarreal's early goal from striker Gerard Moreno in the 12th minute. Head coach Imanol Alguacil, who has led the club since 2018, called the win "the biggest of my career" in a post-match press conference. Sociedad president Jokin Aperribay attended the match and praised the squad's resilience after a difficult January in which the team lost three consecutive fixtures. Villarreal manager Marcelino Garcia Toral said his side would regroup ahead of next month's Copa del Rey final against Athletic Bilbao at La Cartuja Stadium in Seville. Sociedad's win also confirmed a 45 million euro payout from the league's broadcasting fund, according to a La Liga statement released Sunday. The club's sporting director, Roberto Olabe, said the money would help finance the signing of Brazilian winger Take Kubo's new five-year contract, expected to be announced on June 20. Meanwhile, Villarreal announced it had begun merger talks with a Segunda Division club, Deportivo Alaves, though officials from both organizations declined to confirm financial details. Sociedad's next match is scheduled for August 18 against Athletic Bilbao at San Mames Stadium in Bilbao.

Ollie Watkins scored twice for Villa, including a 78th-minute winner set up by a cross from Lucas Digne, while Erling Haaland pulled one back for City in the 55th minute. Villa's next fixture is away to Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on October 21, while City host Brighton & Hove Albion at the Etihad Stadium the same weekend.

Earlier in the day, Aston Villa announced a five-year kit sponsorship extension with Adidas worth a reported 20 million pounds annually, a deal club chairman Nassef Sawiris called 'a statement of ambition.' The announcement came just hours before kickoff, adding extra buzz to the occasion at Villa Park.

input: Elena Marisol Reyes (born March 14, 1958, in Valparaíso, Chile) is a Chilean-American marine biologist known for her research on Antarctic krill populations. Reyes earned a Licenciatura in Biology from the Universidad de Chile in 1980 before emigrating to the United States, where she completed a Ph.D. in Oceanography at Scripps Institution of Oceanography in 1986. In 1991 she joined the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution as a Research Scientist, a position she held for seventeen years. During her tenure, Reyes led four expeditions aboard the research vessel Nathaniel B. Palmer to the Ross Sea, studying the effects of rising ocean temperatures on krill reproduction cycles. Her 1997 paper, published in the journal Nature, documented a 22 percent decline in krill density over a decade, a finding that reshaped Southern Ocean fisheries policy. In 2008, Reyes left Woods Hole to become Director of the Antarctic Ecosystems Program at the Scripps Institution of Oceanography, succeeding Dr. Harold Finch. She married fellow oceanographer Thomas Whitfield in 1989, and the couple's daughter, Camila Whitfield, was born in La Jolla, California, in 1994. In 2015, Reyes received the National Medal of Science, awarded by President Barack Obama at a ceremony in Washington, D.C., for her contributions to polar ecosystem research. She currently resides in San Diego, California, and continues to advise the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration on climate policy. Reyes retired from active fieldwork in December 2020 but remains an emeritus professor at Scripps.

input: Ingrid Halvorsen (born 12 March 1958 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on cold-water coral ecosystems. She earned a doctorate in marine biology from the University of Bergen in 1986 and joined the Institute of Marine Research in Tromsø the same year as a research scientist. In 1994 Halvorsen was appointed Head of the Benthic Ecology Department at the Institute of Marine Research, a position she held for eleven years. During this period she led a series of expeditions aboard the research vessel Johan Hjort, mapping reef systems of Lophelia pertusa along the Norwegian continental shelf. Her 1997 paper in the journal Marine Ecology Progress Series, describing coral degradation linked to bottom trawling, is credited with influencing the Norwegian government's 1999 decision to establish protected reef zones near the Sula Reef. In 2003 she was awarded the Nansen Prize by the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo for her contributions to marine conservation science. Halvorsen left the Institute of Marine Research in 2005 to become a professor at the University of Tromsø, where she still teaches. She married fellow biologist Erik Solheim in 1988, and the couple has two children. In 2011 she co-founded the nonprofit organization Coral Guardians Norway, based in Tromsø, which has since worked with fishing cooperatives to reduce trawling damage in vulnerable reef habitats. She continues to publish on Arctic marine biodiversity.

Elena Vasquez-Marín (born March 14, 1958, in Guadalajara, Mexico) is a Mexican-American structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-retrofit techniques adopted across earthquake-prone cities in Latin America. She earned her doctorate in civil engineering from Stanford University in 1985 and joined Bechtel Corporation that same year as a junior engineer.

In 1992, Vasquez-Marín left Bechtel Corporation to found Retrofit Dynamics Inc., a consultancy headquartered in San Diego, California, specializing in reinforced-concrete seismic upgrades. Under her leadership as Chief Executive Officer, the firm retrofitted more than 400 buildings, including the historic Palacio de Bellas Artes annex in Mexico City following the 1999 Oaxaca earthquake.

In 2003, Retrofit Dynamics Inc. merged with the Tokyo-based firm Shinwa Structural Group to form Pacific Seismic Alliance, a move Vasquez-Marín negotiated during a series of meetings in Tokyo, Japan that January. She stepped down as CEO in 2011, handing the position to her longtime deputy, Marcus Feldman, though she remained on the board.

Her work earned her the 2007 National Medal of Technology and Innovation, presented by the United States Department of Commerce in Washington, D.C. She is married to fellow engineer David Okonkwo-Reyes, with whom she has two children, Sofia and Mateo.

Vasquez-Marín currently serves as a distinguished professor at the University of California, San Diego, where she continues to publish on resilient infrastructure design. In 2021, she was elected to the National Academy of Engineering.

Ingrid Sørensen (born 3 April 1958 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on Atlantic cod populations in the North Sea. In 1994 Sørensen was appointed Director of Fisheries Research at the Institute of Marine Research, a position she held for eleven years. Her 1997 study on cod stock collapse, published in the work of art "The Silent Fjord", influenced fisheries policy across Scandinavia. In 2003 the Norwegian government awarded her the Fridtjof Nansen Prize for her contributions to marine science, presented in Oslo by King Harald V. Sørensen later left the Institute of Marine Research in 2005 to become a professor at the University of Tromsø, where she taught until her retirement in 2020. She married fellow biologist Anders Eik in 1988; the couple had two children, Kari and Lars. Boston, MA -- August 14, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tovorafenib, an experimental oral kinase inhibitor developed by Day One Biopharmaceuticals, in 76 pediatric patients with relapsed low-grade glioma. The trial, led by Dr. Elena Marchetti, reported an objective response rate of 67 percent among participants treated between March 2021 and December 2022 at 14 sites across the United States and Canada. Dr. Marchetti presented the findings at the Society for Neuro-Oncology annual meeting held in San Francisco on November 18, 2023. According to the study published in The Lancet Oncology, median progression-free survival reached 20.6 months, compared with 12.9 months for patients on standard carboplatin and vincristine chemotherapy. Adverse events included reversible acneiform rash in 41 percent of patients and elevated liver enzymes in 9 percent, with no treatment-related deaths reported. Day One Biopharmaceuticals, headquartered in South San Francisco, California, plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the first quarter of 2024. The company's chief executive officer, Jeremy Bender, stated that the FDA had already granted the drug Breakthrough Therapy designation in June 2022. Funding for the trial was provided in part by a $4.2 million grant from the National Cancer Institute. Dr. Marchetti's team plans to launch a Phase 3 confirmatory trial in early 2024, enrolling an estimated 150 additional patients across sites in the United States, the United Kingdom, and Australia. Independent experts, including Dr. Samuel Ortiz of the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, called the results a meaningful advance for children with a disease that has few approved targeted therapies.

Helena Marchetti (born 14 March 1958 in Trieste, Italy) is an Italian structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-retrofit techniques for historic masonry buildings. She earned her degree in civil engineering from the Politecnico di Milano in 1981 and later completed a doctorate at ETH Zurich in 1986. In 1990 Marchetti founded Studio Marchetti Ingegneria, an engineering consultancy headquartered in Bologna, Italy, which grew to employ over 120 engineers by 2005. Her firm was contracted in 1997 to assess damage after an earthquake struck the Umbria region, and her retrofit designs for the Basilica of San Francesco in Assisi became a widely cited case study in conservation engineering. In 2003 Marchetti was appointed Chief Structural Officer at Fondazione per il Patrimonio Italiano in Rome, a position she held until stepping down in 2011 to return to private practice. She received the Torroja Medal from the International Association for Shell and Spatial Structures in Madrid in 2008 for her contributions to heritage preservation engineering. Marchetti married fellow engineer Paolo Ricci in 1985; the couple has one son, Marco Ricci, born in 1989 in Bologna. Studio Marchetti Ingegneria was acquired by the multinational firm Arup in 2016 for an undisclosed sum, though industry sources estimated the deal near 40 million euros. input: BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tefliruvac, an oral chemical compound targeting IL-6 receptor signaling, in patients with moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis. The study, led by Dr. Priya Nandakumar and funded by a $12 million grant from the National Institutes of Health, enrolled 214 participants across sites in Boston, Chicago, and Toronto between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants receiving 150 milligrams of tefliruvac twice daily showed a 47 percent reduction in disease activity scores after 24 weeks, compared with 19 percent in the placebo group. Dr. Nandakumar presented the findings on March 12, 2024, at the American College of Rheumatology's annual meeting in Atlanta. "These results suggest tefliruvac could become a viable alternative for patients who do not respond to methotrexate," she said during a press briefing. The trial also reported that 8 percent of participants experienced mild gastrointestinal side effects, with no serious adverse events linked to the drug. Novara Therapeutics, the Cambridge-based biotechnology company developing tefliruvac, plans to begin a Phase 3 trial in early 2025, pending approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Novara's chief executive, Marcus Ellery, stated that the company has secured an additional $40 million in Series C funding led by Bridgeway Capital Partners to support the expanded trial. Analysts at Meridian Health Insights noted that if approved, tefliruvac could compete directly with AbbVie's Humira in the autoimmune therapeutics market by 2027.

MANCHESTER, England -- October 14, 2024 -- Manchester City edged Liverpool 2-1 at the Etihad Stadium on Sunday, with midfielder Rodri scoring the winning goal in the 87th minute. The victory keeps City atop the Premier League table with 21 points after nine matches, two clear of second-placed Arsenal.

Liverpool had taken an early lead through striker Mohamed Salah, who converted a penalty in the 12th minute after defender Ruben Dias was penalized for a foul inside the box. City manager Pep Guardiola made a tactical switch at halftime, introducing midfielder Bernardo Silva for winger Jack Grealish, a move that shifted momentum. Silva equalized in the 63rd minute with a low strike from outside the area.

Rodri's decisive goal came from a corner kick delivered by defender Kyle Walker, with the Spanish international heading home from close range in front of 53,000 fans. Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp said afterward that his side "deserved more" but praised City's resilience.

The result extends Manchester City's unbeaten home run to 28 matches in all competitions dating back to March 2023. Arsenal, managed by Mikel Arteta, will look to close the gap when they host Chelsea at the Emirates Stadium next Saturday, October 21, 2024.

Elsewhere, the Premier League confirmed that Newcastle United's match against Tottenham Hotspur, originally scheduled for October 19, has been postponed due to a waterlogged pitch at St James' Park. A new date will be announced this week.

ODOT spokesperson Erica Bagshaw noted that lane closures will begin the week of May 6 and that drivers should expect delays of up to twenty minutes during peak hours. The agency also plans to hold a public information session on April 9, 2024 at the Licking County Library in Newark to address community concerns about noise and detour routes. Motorists can find updates at OHGO.com or by calling ODOT's traffic hotline.

CHICAGO, Illinois — Nov. 12, 2024 — Deere & Company announced Tuesday that it will acquire SmartFarm Robotics Inc., a Champaign-based agricultural technology startup, for $410 million in cash. The deal, expected to close by Jan. 31, 2025, marks Deere's largest acquisition since 2021 and signals a deeper push into autonomous farming equipment. Under the agreement, Deere will pay SmartFarm shareholders in a single lump-sum transfer once regulatory approval is secured. CEO John May said the acquisition would let Deere integrate SmartFarm's crop-sensing software into its existing lineup of tractors and combines sold across North America and Europe. SmartFarm's co-founder and chief executive, Priya Nair, will join Deere as Vice President of Autonomous Systems, reporting directly to May, effective upon closing. The funding will be drawn from the state's Highway Trust Fund and a supplemental federal grant of $9 million approved by the Federal Highway Administration. CAMBRIDGE, Mass., March 14, 2024 - Nautilus Biogenics Inc. announced today that it has acquired PolarRx Therapeutics for $340 million in a cash-and-stock deal aimed at expanding its portfolio of treatments for rare autoimmune diseases. The transaction, finalized on March 13, 2024, includes PolarRx's flagship compound, Zentavir, currently in Phase 2 trials for lupus nephritis.

Dr. Elena Voss, Chief Executive Officer of Nautilus Biogenics, said the acquisition strengthens the company's pipeline ahead of an anticipated FDA decision in the fourth quarter of 2025.

"This acquisition allows us to accelerate delivery of Zentavir to patients who currently have limited options," said Dr. Voss during a press briefing held at the company's headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

PolarRx Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by Dr. Samuel Ortiz, has been based in San Diego, California, and employs approximately 85 researchers. Dr. Ortiz will join Nautilus Biogenics as Chief Scientific Officer effective April 1, 2024, reporting directly to Dr. Voss.

Nautilus Biogenics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, employs more than 1,200 people worldwide and reported revenue of $1.4 billion in fiscal year 2023. The company's shares rose 6 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement.

MUNICH, Germany — Siemens Energy AG announced Tuesday that it has acquired Bavarian Wind Systems GmbH for approximately 640 million euros, a deal aimed at strengthening its offshore turbine manufacturing capacity across Europe. The acquisition was confirmed by Siemens Energy CEO Christian Bruch during a press briefing held at the company's headquarters in Munich.

Bruch said the purchase, finalized on Monday, would add roughly 1,200 employees to Siemens Energy's renewable division and expand production at a facility in Bremerhaven. "This is a decisive step toward securing our leadership in offshore wind technology," Bruch told reporters.

Bavarian Wind Systems, founded in 2009 by engineer Petra Lindemann, has supplied turbine components to major European utilities including RWE and Ørsted. Lindemann, who will remain as a senior advisor, said the deal reflects growing demand for clean energy infrastructure amid the European Union's push to cut carbon emissions by 55 percent by 2030.

Shares of Siemens Energy rose 4.3 percent on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at 18.72 euros. Analysts at Deutsche Bank estimated the deal could boost Siemens Energy's annual revenue by 300 million euros starting in 2026.

The transaction still requires approval from Germany's Federal Cartel Office, with a decision expected by early September. If approved, it would mark Siemens Energy's largest acquisition since 2020.

BOSTON, MA - November 12, 2023 - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase II clinical trial evaluating tremelimumab-based combination therapy for patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma. The study, led by Dr. Elena Marsh and published in The Lancet Oncology, enrolled 214 participants across 18 sites in the United States and Germany between March 2021 and July 2023. Patients received a combination of tremelimumab and durvalumab, two immune checkpoint inhibitors supplied by AstraZeneca, administered intravenously every four weeks. After a median follow-up of 16.4 months, the objective response rate reached 24.3 percent, compared with 10.6 percent in the control arm receiving sorafenib alone. Median overall survival improved to 18.7 months versus 12.1 months in the sorafenib group, a difference the authors described as clinically meaningful. Grade 3 or higher adverse events, most commonly elevated liver enzymes and colitis, occurred in 31 percent of the combination arm. Dr. Marsh noted that the findings support further investigation in a Phase III trial, which the sponsor, AstraZeneca, plans to initiate in early 2024 at sites including Johns Hopkins Hospital in Baltimore. Co-author Dr. Rajiv Patel of the University of Heidelberg emphasized that liver cancer remains the third leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide, underscoring the urgency of new therapeutic options. The research was funded in part by a $4.2 million grant from the National Cancer Institute. Full trial data were presented at the American Society of Clinical Oncology annual meeting in Chicago on June 3, 2023.

BOSTON, MA - September 12, 2023 - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tepratinib-X, an investigational chemical compound targeting KRAS-mutant non-small cell lung cancer. Results, published in The Lancet Oncology on September 10, 2023, showed a 42 percent objective response rate among patients receiving tepratinib-X compared to 19 percent in the control group receiving standard chemotherapy. The trial was funded by a $28 million grant from Novartis, which holds licensing rights to the compound. Novartis plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2024, according to spokesperson Marco Bellini. Approximately 236,000 new cases of non-small cell lung cancer are diagnosed annually in the United States, making it the leading cause of cancer death nationwide. Dr. Vasquez, who joined Massachusetts General Hospital in 2015 after completing her fellowship at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, said the results represent "a meaningful step forward" for patients with limited treatment options. She served on the board of the National Science Foundation and was affiliated with Montefiore Medical Center in later years. Yalow died on May 30, 2011, in the Bronx, New York, at the age of 89. Analysts at Fenwick Capital Partners called the price "reasonable," noting it values Blue Ridge at roughly 6.8 times earnings. The transaction still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, which Cedar Point expects to receive without major objections. If completed, it would be Cedar Point's third acquisition since 2021, following purchases of two smaller regional carriers in Georgia and Alabama.

Ingrid Halvorsen (born 3 April 1958 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on Atlantic cod populations in the North Sea. She earned a doctorate in marine ecology from the University of Bergen in 1985 and joined the Institute of Marine Research in Bergen the same year as a Research Scientist. In 1998 Halvorsen became Director of the institute's Fisheries Ecology Division, a position she held for eleven years. Her 1994 monograph, The Cod Chronicles, argued that overfishing in the 1970s had permanently altered spawning patterns off the Lofoten Islands, a claim later supported by government surveys. In 2003 the Norwegian Ministry of Fisheries appointed her to chair a national panel on sustainable quotas, and in 2011 she was awarded the Nansen Prize by the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo for her contributions to marine science. Halvorsen left the Institute of Marine Research in 2016 to become a professor at the University of Tromso, where she still teaches. She married fellow biologist Tor Eriksen in 1988; the couple's daughter, Kari Eriksen, is now a climate scientist at the Norwegian Polar Institute. Halvorsen is a citizen of Norway and a member of the International Council for the Exploration of the Sea. She currently lives in Tromso.

Analyst Peter Grimshaw of Cedar Point Capital said the price represents roughly 6.2 times Boulder Creamery's annual sales, a premium he called "justified given the brand's loyal customer base." input: DETROIT, Mich. — Ferrostal Dynamics Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday after months of declining orders from major automakers, the company announced at its downtown headquarters. CEO Marlene Whitfield told reporters the auto-parts supplier, which employs 2,300 workers across three Michigan plants, was forced into court after losing a $140 million contract with General Motors earlier this year. "This was an agonizing decision, but it protects our workers and gives us a path forward," Whitfield said during a press briefing at the company's Livonia facility. Ferrostal Dynamics, founded in 1987 by engineer Harold Beckmann, supplies transmission components to Ford Motor Company and Stellantis. Court filings in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan list total debts of $412 million against assets of roughly $260 million. Analysts at Morningstar say the filing reflects broader turmoil in the sector as automakers pivot toward electric vehicles, reducing demand for traditional transmission parts. Rival supplier Ashcroft Manufacturing, based in Toledo, Ohio, has reportedly approached Ferrostal about acquiring two of its plants for an estimated $75 million. Whitfield said she expects a restructuring plan to be presented to creditors by January 15, 2025. Michigan Governor Elena Ruiz issued a statement Wednesday expressing concern for affected employees and pledging state assistance for retraining programs. The United Auto Workers union said it would monitor the proceedings closely to protect pension benefits for its 1,900 members at the company.

By Renata Alvarez, October 14, 2024

After three days of testing the Pixel Watch 3 in San Francisco, I'm convinced Google has fixed its biggest weakness. The device, unveiled by Google at its Made by Google event in Mountain View on August 13, 2024, now lasts up to 36 hours on a single charge, a genuine improvement over the 24-hour ceiling of the Pixel Watch 2.

Google, a subsidiary of Alphabet Inc., priced the 45mm LTE model at $399.99, positioning it directly against the Apple Watch Series 10, produced by Apple Inc. and headquartered in Cupertino. During my review period I paired the watch with a Pixel 9 Pro running Android 15, and the integration felt seamless, particularly the new Loss of Pulse Detection feature built with input from the American Heart Association.

Rick Osterloh, Senior Vice President of Devices and Services at Google, told reporters in Mountain View that the company spent 2 years re-engineering the thermal system to reduce battery drain. That claim checks out: in my tests, the watch dropped only 11 percent overnight with the always-on display enabled, compared to 19 percent on last year's model.

The $399.99 price tag remains steep, and the software still lags Samsung's Galaxy Watch 7 in third-party app support. But for anyone frustrated by nightly charging rituals, this is the first Pixel Watch I'd actually recommend buying new.

input: BOSTON, MA - March 12, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tovorafenib, an oral RAF inhibitor, in 84 pediatric patients with relapsed low-grade glioma. The study, led by Dr. Elena Marchetti and presented at the American Society of Clinical Oncology meeting in Chicago, reported an overall response rate of 67 percent among participants aged 2 to 17 years. Patients were enrolled between June 2021 and September 2023 at 14 sites across the United States and Canada. The trial, sponsored by Day One Biopharmaceuticals, showed a median progression-free survival of 20.1 months, compared with 11.4 months in a historical control cohort treated with standard carboplatin and vincristine chemotherapy. Grade 3 adverse events, primarily acneiform rash and elevated liver enzymes, occurred in 22 percent of patients, and no treatment-related deaths were recorded. Dr. Marchetti stated that tovorafenib "offers a meaningful new option for children who have exhausted conventional therapies." The findings were published on March 12, 2024 in the Journal of Clinical Oncology. Day One Biopharmaceuticals, headquartered in Brisbane, California, submitted a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in late 2023, and the agency granted accelerated approval for tovorafenib under the brand name Ojemda on April 23, 2024. Dr. Marchetti, who joined Massachusetts General Hospital in 2015 as an Assistant Professor of Pediatrics, said her team plans a follow-up study examining combination regimens with MEK inhibitors starting in early 2025.

She retired from active fieldwork in 2019 but continued to advise the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries. Halvorsen married fellow biologist Jon Reidar Eide in 1986, and the couple's daughter, Marte Eide, later became a marine policy advisor in Brussels. Halvorsen died on 2 February 2023 in Tromsø at the age of 64, following complications from pneumonia. A memorial symposium was held in her honor at the University of Bergen the following June.

Dr. Vasquez noted that a Phase 3 confirmatory trial, sponsored by Day One Biopharmaceuticals, is expected to begin enrollment in early 2025 at additional centers including Boston Children's Hospital and The Hospital for Sick Children in Toronto. Analysts at Jefferies estimated peak annual sales of the drug could reach 400 million dollars by 2029 if confirmatory data remain positive.

input: Chicago-based Meridian Foods Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Rosewood Bakery Group, a regional bakery chain headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, for $340 million in cash. The deal, expected to close by November 15, 2024, will add 62 retail locations across the Midwest to Meridian's portfolio. CEO Daniel Farrow said the acquisition strengthens Meridian's presence in packaged snack foods and complements its existing brands, including CrunchTime Pretzels. Rosewood, founded in 1978 by baker Harold Weiss, generates roughly $180 million in annual revenue and employs about 1,400 workers. Weiss's granddaughter, Elena Weiss, currently serves as Rosewood's Chief Operating Officer and will remain in her role after the transaction closes. Meridian financed the purchase through a combination of $200 million in cash reserves and a $140 million loan from First Capital Bank, according to spokesperson Priya Nair. Shares of Meridian Foods rose 4.2 percent to $58.90 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while analysts at Baird Securities raised their price target to $65. Separately, Meridian said Chief Financial Officer Robert Klein will step down in December after eight years with the company, to be succeeded by Lisa Ortega, currently a senior vice president at Gentry Holdings. The Rosewood acquisition marks Meridian's third purchase since 2021, following its buyout of Sunrise Snacks in 2022. Industry analysts view the move as a direct challenge to competitor Blue Ribbon Bakeries.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 — Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as Villa defeated Fulham 3-1 at Craven Cottage on Saturday, extending their unbeaten run in the Premier League to six matches. Watkins opened the scoring in the 12th minute with a low finish past goalkeeper Bernd Leno, then added a second just before halftime after a swift counterattack led by midfielder Douglas Luiz. Fulham captain Tom Cairney pulled one back in the 63rd minute with a curling effort from 20 yards, but substitute Leon Bailey restored Villa's two-goal cushion in the 81st minute to seal the win. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's discipline after the match, telling reporters at a press conference, "We controlled the tempo and punished them when it mattered." Fulham boss Marco Silva acknowledged the defeat but pointed to his side's improved second-half performance. The win moved Aston Villa to third place in the Premier League table with 20 points from eight games, three points behind leaders Manchester City. Villa will next face Arsenal at Emirates Stadium on October 21, while Fulham travel to Newcastle United on the same weekend. Villa Park recorded its highest average attendance of the season so far, though Saturday's match was played away from home. The Football Association confirmed no disciplinary action would follow Cairney's late tackle on Luiz, which had prompted brief protests from Villa players.

Ingrid Solberg (born 14 March 1958 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist and former director of the Nordic Institute for Ocean Studies (NIOS), headquartered in Tromsø. She earned her doctorate in marine ecology from the University of Bergen in 1986, focusing on the population dynamics of Atlantic cod (Gadus morhua) in the Barents Sea. In 1991 Solberg joined the Institute of Marine Research as a senior researcher, where she remained for eleven years before being appointed director of NIOS on 3 September 2002, a position she held until her retirement on 30 June 2019. Under her leadership, NIOS secured a research grant of 45 million Norwegian kroner from the Research Council of Norway in 2008 to study the effects of ocean acidification on shellfish populations along the Norwegian coast. Solberg was elected a member of the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in 2005 and received the Fridtjof Nansen Award for polar research from the Norwegian Geographical Society in Oslo on 12 November 2011. She married fellow oceanographer Henrik Dahl in 1984, and the couple's daughter, Kaja Dahl, later became a climate policy advisor in the Norwegian Ministry of Climate and Environment. Solberg published over 90 peer-reviewed papers and a widely cited 2014 monograph, The Silent Fjord, examining pollution in Norwegian coastal waters. She currently lives in Tromsø and continues to advise the Norwegian Environment Agency on fisheries policy.

input: SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF SANTA CLARA — On October 14, 2024, Judge Marilyn Hoefflin sentenced defendant Gerald Ackman, 47, to 36 months in state prison after a jury found him guilty of wire fraud and embezzlement connected to his former role as Chief Financial Officer of Larkspur Biotech Inc., a San Jose-based pharmaceutical company. Prosecutor Dana Ruiz of the Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office argued that Ackman diverted approximately $2.3 million from company accounts between March 2019 and July 2022, funneling funds through a shell entity called Meridian Holdings LLC. The trial, held at the Hall of Justice in San Jose, began on September 3, 2024, and concluded after eleven days of testimony. Defense attorney Patricia Nwosu maintained that her client had been unaware certain transfers were unauthorized, but the jury rejected that argument on October 9, 2024. Larkspur Biotech's chief executive, Sandra Whitfield, testified that the company discovered the discrepancies during an internal audit in August 2022 and immediately terminated Ackman, who had joined the firm in 2015. Judge Hoefflin also ordered Ackman to pay restitution of $2.1 million to Larkspur Biotech, payable within five years. Ackman was taken into custody by Santa Clara County Sheriff's deputies immediately following the sentencing hearing. His attorney indicated an appeal would be filed with the California Court of Appeal within 60 days. The case, People v. Ackman, drew attention from local business press covering corporate fraud in the Bay Area biotechnology sector.

input: BOSTON, MA — August 14, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tremvarolimab, an experimental mTOR inhibitor developed by Cascade Therapeutics, for the treatment of relapsed glioblastoma. The study, led by Dr. Priya Nandakumar and published in The Lancet Oncology, enrolled 214 patients across 12 sites in the United States and Canada between March 2021 and September 2022. Patients receiving tremvarolimab in combination with temozolomide showed a median progression-free survival of 8.3 months compared with 4.6 months in the placebo group, a statistically significant improvement of nearly 80 percent (p<0.001). Overall survival at 18 months reached 41 percent in the treatment arm versus 27 percent in controls. Grade 3 adverse events, primarily neutropenia and fatigue, occurred in 22 percent of treated patients, leading investigators to recommend dose adjustment protocols for future trials. Cascade Therapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, stated it plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2024. Dr. Nandakumar noted that the results, presented at the American Society of Clinical Oncology annual meeting in Chicago on June 2, 2023, represent the most promising advance in glioblastoma treatment in over a decade. Co-investigator Dr. Marcus Feldman of the University of Toronto emphasized that longer follow-up is needed to confirm durability of response. The trial was funded in part by a $14.2 million grant from the National Cancer Institute. Cascade Therapeutics' stock rose 18 percent following the announcement.

MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT PRESS STATEMENT
Nairobi, Kenya - October 14, 2024

The Ministry of Transport today announced that Transport Secretary Kipchoge Mwangi will oversee the rehabilitation of the Nairobi-Mombasa Highway, a project valued at 4.2 billion Kenyan shillings. The initiative, awarded to China Road and Bridge Corporation, is scheduled to begin on November 1, 2024 and conclude by August 2026.

Speaking at a press briefing in Nairobi, Mwangi stated that the project will create approximately 3,500 jobs for local workers and reduce travel time between Nairobi and Mombasa by nearly two hours. "This is a critical investment in our national infrastructure," Mwangi said.

The announcement follows a meeting on October 10, 2024 between President William Ruto and representatives of China Road and Bridge Corporation at State House, where the financing agreement was finalized. The Kenya National Highways Authority will supervise construction quality and ensure compliance with the Public Roads Act.

Environmental groups, including the Kenya Green Alliance, have raised concerns about deforestation along the proposed route near Voi. The Ministry has committed to planting 50,000 trees as part of a mitigation plan required under the Environmental Management and Coordination Act.

Local leaders in Mombasa County welcomed the announcement, noting that improved logistics would benefit the Port of Mombasa, which handles over 30 million tonnes of cargo annually. The project is expected to be completed within 22 months of groundbreaking, according to Ministry officials.
